ai.description: *Minervarya sahyadris* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown-mottled dorsum and white belly. It is distinguished by a prominent mid-dorsal ridge and distinct, interrupted longitudinal skin folds.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya sahyadris* is best identified by the distinct, continuous, and prominent glandular fold running along the sides of its back, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya sahyadris* inhabits the Western Ghats, typically found in high-altitude montane grasslands and marshy areas near seasonal pools and rocky streams.
ai.behavior: *Minervarya sahyadris* is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small insects and invertebrates among the leaf litter of its forest floor habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya sahyadris* is an oviparous breeder that lays clutches of 100–200 eggs in shallow water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya sahyadris* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Kerala at low to mid-elevations.
ai.callDescription: The *Minervarya sahyadris* produces a high-pitched, insect-like buzzing call consisting of a rapid series of pulses, typically heard in wet, grassy habitats during monsoon.
